study: Massively parallel phenotyping of coding variants in cancer with Perturb-seq
target_scope: TP53 and KRAS coding variants (~200 variant constructs)
tf_focus: Partial (TP53 is a TF; KRAS not)
relevance_notes: THE canonical large Perturb-seq in A549 lung line; variant-level ORF effects on transcriptome. Directly relevant to lung TF/oncogene perturbation.

study: Single-cell CRISPRi transcriptome screening of hypoxia-regulated lncRNAs in LUAD
relevance_notes: Lung adenocarcinoma single-cell CRISPRi; small library (lncRNA not TF) but genuine lung perturbation dataset.

study: Massively multiplex chemical transcriptomics at single-cell resolution (sci-Plex)
relevance_notes: A549 included; chemical (not genetic) perturbation. Useful as A549 drug-response reference, not TF-KO. sci-Plex backbone.

study: Identification of required host factors for SARS-CoV-2 infection (A549)
relevance_notes: A549 single-cell CRISPR (host-factor focus, not TF). Included for completeness of A549 perturbation catalog.

study: A transcription factor atlas of directed differentiation
method: ORF-overexpression atlas + scRNA-seq (+ SHARE-seq RNA/ATAC subset)
target_scope: All annotated human TF splice isoforms (>3,500 TF ORFs)
data_availability: Public (processed h5ad on Zenodo/Broad SCP; GEO raw)
relevance_notes: The definitive pan-TF overexpression atlas. Directly the 'TF library' the project centers on; matched RNA+ATAC (SHARE-seq) subset makes it multiomic. Prime reprogramming reference.

study: Coupled single-cell CRISPR screening and epigenomic profiling reveals causal gene regulatory networks (Perturb-ATAC)
target_scope: Chromatin/TF regulators in keratinocytes & B/GM12878 (tens of targets)
relevance_notes: First coupled CRISPR + single-cell chromatin method; directly builds TF→chromatin causal GRNs — the methodological template for the project's multiomic GRN aim.

study: High-throughput single-cell chromatin accessibility CRISPR screens (Spear-ATAC)
target_scope: Up to ~35+ TFs/chromatin factors per screen (GATA1, TFs)
relevance_notes: Scalable perturbation→chromatin readout. TF perturbations with direct accessibility effects; scalable template for lung TF-ATAC screens.

study: Simultaneous single-cell CRISPR, RNA, and ATAC-seq for multiomic CRISPR screens
method: Tri-modal single-cell (sgRNA + RNA + ATAC same cell)
relevance_notes: Genuine single-cell tri-modal perturbation (CRISPR+RNA+ATAC same cell) built explicitly to infer gene-regulatory relationships — the exact modality the project prioritizes.

study: Multimodal pooled Perturb-CITE-seq screens in patient models define mechanisms of cancer immune evasion
tf_focus: Partial (includes TFs e.g. in IFN response)
relevance_notes: Large multimodal (RNA+protein) perturbation screen; TF/IFN pathway targets. Distributed via Broad SCP, not GEO.

study: Characterizing the molecular regulation of inhibitory immune checkpoints with multimodal single-cell screens (ECCITE-seq / Mixscape)
relevance_notes: Defines Mixscape workflow; TF regulators of checkpoint expression. Multimodal RNA+protein reference.

study: Transcription factor dynamics, oscillation, and functions in human enteroendocrine cell differentiation
relevance_notes: TF-driven differentiation with matched multiome; a template for TF→(RNA+ATAC) mapping in an epithelial lineage (transferable logic to lung epithelium).

study: Dissecting gene regulatory networks governing human cortical cell fate
relevance_notes: Human+macaque GRN dissection with perturbation and multiome — directly models the mouse/human GRN-comparison and fate-TF logic the project targets (in cortex; transferable framework).

study: Scalable, multimodal profiling of chromatin accessibility, gene expression and protein levels (DOGMA-seq / ASAP-seq)
relevance_notes: Tri-modal single-cell method that can be coupled to CRISPR; establishes the RNA+ATAC+protein readout the project could adopt for lung.

study: Mapping information-rich genotype-phenotype landscapes with genome-scale Perturb-seq
target_scope: Genome-scale: all expressed genes (~9,800 in K562 GWPS) + essential-gene screens (K562, RPE1)
relevance_notes: The reference genome-scale Perturb-seq. Contains every TF as a perturbation → essential backbone for cross-cell-type TF-regulon comparison. Processed matrices downloadable from figshare.

study: Perturb-Seq: Dissecting molecular circuits with scalable single-cell RNA profiling of pooled genetic screens
tf_focus: YES (original screen targeted TFs in BMDCs)
relevance_notes: Founding Perturb-seq paper; BMDC screen targeted TFs — early TF-regulon inference proof of concept.

study: A multiplexed single-cell CRISPR screening platform enables systematic dissection of the unfolded protein response
relevance_notes: Foundational multiplexed Perturb-seq; UPR TFs (ATF6, XBP1). Establishes barcode-guide pairing.

study: Dissecting immune circuits by linking CRISPR-pooled screens with single-cell RNA-seq (CRISP-seq)
relevance_notes: Founding immune Perturb-seq with TF targets; mouse system → relevant for mouse/human comparison of immune TF circuits.

study: Pooled CRISPR screening with single-cell transcriptome read-out (CROP-seq)
relevance_notes: Introduced CROP-seq (guide in polyA transcript) — the vector design most lung screens still use.

study: Exploring genetic interaction manifolds constructed from rich single-cell phenotypes
target_scope: ~112 single + ~131 dual perturbations of differentiation/TF genes
relevance_notes: Combinatorial CRISPRa of TFs → genetic-interaction manifold. Directly models the 'TF combination' logic for the reprogramming aim (which pairs synergize).

study: Combinatorial single-cell CRISPR screens by direct guide RNA capture and targeted sequencing
relevance_notes: Direct guide-capture enabling combinatorial/CRISPRi screens; underpins genome-scale work.

study: Targeted Perturb-seq enables genome-scale genetic screens in single cells (TAP-seq)
relevance_notes: Targeted readout drastically cuts cost — practical option for large lung TF screens focused on regulon genes.

study: Scalable genetic screening for regulatory circuits using compressed Perturb-seq
relevance_notes: Compressed sensing cuts cells needed for large libraries — directly relevant to scaling a TF-library screen in lung economically.

study: In vivo Perturb-Seq reveals neuronal and glial abnormalities associated with autism risk genes
relevance_notes: First in vivo Perturb-seq; template for in vivo lung perturbation. Mouse system for cross-species logic.

study: Massively parallel in vivo Perturb-seq reveals cell-type-specific transcriptional networks in cortical development
relevance_notes: Cell-type-specific TF networks in development via in vivo perturbation — directly analogous to the project's developmental-trajectory TF-network aim (in cortex).

study: CRISPR interference-based platform for multimodal genetic screens in human iPSC-derived neurons
relevance_notes: CRISPRi in differentiated (non-cancer) human cells — model for perturbing mature/differentiated lung cell states rather than cancer lines.

study: Single-cell RNA-sequencing-based CRISPRi screening resolves molecular drivers of early human endoderm development
relevance_notes: TF CRISPRi during directed differentiation — endoderm gives rise to lung; directly relevant developmental-TF logic for lung reprogramming.

study: Discovery of target genes and pathways at GWAS loci by pooled single-cell CRISPR screens (STING-seq)
relevance_notes: Links noncoding variants to target genes at single-cell resolution — method template for connecting lung GWAS/enhancers to TF regulons.

study: scPerturb: harmonized single-cell perturbation data
relevance_notes: Harmonized, standardized h5ad for ~50 perturbation datasets incl. many above. THE most efficient way to pull analysis-ready processed matrices; use to grab specific datasets without re-processing.

study: Dissecting cell identity via network inference and in silico gene perturbation (CellOracle)
method: Computational: GRN inference + in silico TF perturbation (from scRNA+scATAC)
relevance_notes: Exactly the in-silico TF-perturbation/GRN engine the project describes: infers GRN from multiome, simulates KO/OE to predict fate shifts. Pair with Perturb-seq for validation.

study: Predicting transcriptional outcomes of novel multigene perturbations with GEARS
relevance_notes: Predicts combinatorial perturbation outcomes — supports choosing which TF KO/OE combinations to test for reprogramming. Trained on Norman/Replogle Perturb-seq.

study: SCENIC+: single-cell multiomic inference of enhancers and gene regulatory networks
method: Computational: enhancer-driven GRN inference from matched scRNA+scATAC
relevance_notes: Third GRN engine alongside CellOracle and GEARS. Infers enhancer-driven TF regulons directly from matched multiome (the modality this program prioritises); complements CellOracle's in-silico KO by adding enhancer/region-level regulatory links. Use to build the lung TF-GRN from matched RNA+ATAC before designing perturbations.
verify_status: Verified: DOI (OpenAlex, Nat Methods 2023, not retracted)

study: Tahoe-100M: A Giga-Scale Single-Cell Perturbation Atlas for Context-Dependent Gene Function
method: Massively parallel single-cell chemical transcriptomics (Mosaic 'cell village')
cell_line: 50 cancer cell lines incl. A549 & HOP-92 (lung)
relevance_notes: THE small-molecule mirroring backbone. 1,100 compound perturbations profiled by scRNA-seq across 50 lines; A549 (DepMap ACH-000681; KRAS-G12S/STK11/SMARCA4/CDKN2A) and HOP-92 are lung. Drug metadata (targets, MoA, SMILES, PubChem CID, human-approved flag) queryable via HuggingFace datasets API. Inaugural contribution to Arc Institute Virtual Cell Atlas (ties to project's virtual-cell-atlas foundation). Use to test whether a TF-combination signature can be mirrored by a compound in A549.
verify_status: Verified: DOI+abstract (OpenAlex/bioRxiv); cell-line & drug metadata pulled from HuggingFace API

study: Single-cell multi-omic atlas and morphogen screening informs midbrain and hindbrain organoid engineering
method: Matched single-cell multiome (RNA+ATAC) + GRN inference + TF perturbation + multiplexed morphogen screen
repository: Publisher / lab (not in GEO as of search)
data_availability: Open access paper; data via publisher/lab
relevance_notes: Conceptual template for external-intervention mirroring. Matched multiome + GRN inference + TF perturbation resolve differentiation, and a multiplexed morphogen-patterning screen shows external cues steering a GRN-defined fate. Directly models 'can a non-genetic intervention reproduce a TF-combination-defined state transition?'. From Treutlein/Camp groups (barbara.treutlein@bsse.ethz.ch).
verify_status: Verified: DOI (OpenAlex, Nat Neurosci 2026, open access, not retracted)

study: A Next Generation Connectivity Map: L1000 Platform and the First 1,000,000 Profiles
approx_size: Very large raw; queried via API (not downloaded)
relevance_notes: The connectivity ENGINE for the small-molecule layer. Given a TF-perturbation up/down signature, rank compounds whose signatures mimic or reverse it (A549 & HCC515 lung signatures available). Queried live via Enrichr / SigCom LINCS APIs (maayanlab.cloud) - no bulk download needed. Validated this session on a real KLF1-CRISPRa signature.
verify_status: Verified: DOI (OpenAlex, Cell 2017, 3,711 cites, not retracted); API reachable

study: The Connectivity Map: Using Gene-Expression Signatures to Connect Small Molecules, Genes, and Disease
method: Reference gene-expression profiles of small-molecule perturbations; signature matching
relevance_notes: Origin of the signature-connectivity paradigm this layer builds on: match a query expression signature to compound signatures to nominate mimicking or reversing drugs. Superseded in scale by L1000/Tahoe but defines the method.
verify_status: Verified: DOI (OpenAlex, Science 2006, 5,475 cites, not retracted)

study: Chromatin and gene-regulatory dynamics of human pulmogenesis by single cell multiomic sequencing (Human Lung Development Atlas, HLDA)
method: Single-cell multiome (10x ARC: matched snRNA + snATAC same nucleus)
target_scope: Whole developing lung (PCW 12-23); 581,745 cCREs, 121,486 peak-to-gene links
tf_focus: Partial (GRN/TF regulatory modules inferred, not perturbed)
cell_line: Primary human fetal lung (not a cell line)
data_availability: Open (CC-BY-NC-ND); processed RNA+ATAC, ArchR/Seurat objects, ChromBPNet models
approx_size: 317 GB full community; ~5.3 GB selected (RNA objects + peaks + matched matrix)
relevance_notes: HIGHEST-VALUE GRN substrate for this program. Matched RNA+ATAC (same nucleus) across human lung development PCW 12-23 with cCREs already linked to genes and TF regulatory modules along differentiation trajectories (aerocyte, arterial, alveolar). This is the observational developmental reference the program's CellOracle/SCENIC+ GRN should be built on BEFORE nominating fate-instructive TFs; epithelial lineage object is the lung-fate focus. Directly enables the 'redirect mature lung state toward developmental trajectory' aim.
verify_status: Verified: DOI+bioRxiv record (Greenleaf/Krasnow, Stanford, 2025-09-25); Zenodo community + file listing retrieved via API
